en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
5. The Question on What is Not Born of Karma, etc.

“Venerable Nāgasena, there are things seen in the world born of karma, there are things seen born of causes, and there are things seen born of season. Tell me, then, what in the world is not born of karma, not born of causes, and not born of season.
“There are these two things, Great King, in the world that are not born of karma, not born of causes, and not born of season.”
Which two?
Space, great king, is not born of karma, not born of a cause, not born of conditions;
Nibbāna, great king, is not born of karma, not born of a cause, not born of conditions.
“Great King, these two are indeed not born of karma, not born of causes, and not born of conditions.
“Venerable Nāgasena, do not defile the word of the Conqueror; do not answer a question without understanding it!
“What is it that I say, Great King, such that you speak to me thus: ‘Venerable Nāgasena, do not defile the word of the Conqueror; do not answer a question without understanding it’?”
“Venerable Nāgasena, it is indeed reasonable to say that ‘space is not born of action, not born of cause, and not born of condition.
But, venerable Nāgasena, for hundreds of reasons the Blessed One has taught disciples the path for the realization of Nibbāna; and yet you say, ‘Nibbāna is not born of cause.
“It is true, Great King, that the Blessed One taught disciples the path for the realization of Nibbāna through hundreds of reasons; however, he did not teach a cause for the arising of Nibbāna.”
“Herein, venerable Nāgasena, we enter from darkness into deeper darkness, from forest into denser forest,
from thicket into thicker thicket, in that there is a cause for the realization of Nibbāna,
yet there is no cause for the arising of that Dhamma.”
"If, venerable Nāgasena, there is a cause for the realization of Nibbāna, then by that same logic, a cause for the arising of Nibbāna must also be accepted.
Just as, venerable Nāgasena, because a son has a father, one must also accept a father for that father;
and just as because a pupil has a teacher, one must also accept a teacher for that teacher."
"Just as a sprout has a seed, for that reason a seed must also be admitted for the seed itself.
Even so, venerable Nāgasena, if there is a cause for the realization of Nibbāna, for that reason a cause for the arising of Nibbāna must also be admitted.
Just as when there is a top to a tree or a creeper, for that reason there is also a middle and a root."
“In the same way, venerable Nāgasena, if there is a cause for the realization of Nibbāna, then for that reason a cause for the arising of Nibbāna should also be expected.
“Nibbāna, Great King, is not something to be produced; therefore, no cause for the arising of Nibbāna has been taught.
“Come now, venerable Nāgasena, show me the reason and convince me with logic, so that I may understand how there is a cause for the realization of Nibbāna, but no cause for the arising of Nibbāna.”

“In that case, Great King, lend your ear attentively and listen well; I shall explain the reason for this. Would a man, Great King, be able to go from here to the Himalayas, the king of mountains, by his ordinary strength?
“Yes, venerable sir.
“But would that man, Great King, be able to bring the Himalayas, the king of mountains, here by his ordinary strength?”
“No indeed, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, it is possible to point out the path for the realization of Nibbāna, but it is not possible to show the cause for the arising of Nibbāna.

Great king, would a man be able, by his ordinary strength, to cross the great ocean by boat and reach the further shore? “No, venerable sir. “In the same way, great king, it is possible to point out the path for the realization of Nibbāna, but it is not possible to show the cause for the arising of Nibbāna.”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“But could that man, O Great King, by his ordinary strength bring the far shore of the great ocean here?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.”
“In the same way, great king, it is possible to describe the path for the realization of Nibbāna, but it is not possible to point out a cause for the arising of Nibbāna.
Why is that? Because of the unconditioned nature of that Dhamma.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes, Great King, Nibbāna is unconditioned; it was not made by anyone.
Nibbāna, Great King, cannot be said to have arisen, nor to be unarisen, nor to be something that can be produced, nor to be past, nor future, nor present.”
“Or whether it is cognizable by the eye, or cognizable by the ear, or cognizable by the nose, or cognizable by the tongue,
or cognizable by the body. “If, venerable Nāgasena, Nibbāna has not arisen, nor is it unarisen, nor is it subject to arising, nor is it past...”
"It is neither future nor present; it is not cognizable by the eye, nor by the ear, nor by the nose, nor by the tongue, nor by the body.
Therefore, venerable Nāgasena, you point to Nibbāna as a non-existent phenomenon, saying, 'Nibbāna does not exist.'"

“There is, Great King, Nibbāna; Nibbāna is cognizable by the mind. A noble disciple who has entered upon the right practice sees Nibbāna with a mind that is purified, sublime, straight, unobstructed, and spiritual.
“But of what kind, Bhante, is that Nibbāna which can be illustrated by similes? Convince me through reasons and similes, for a thing that exists can be illustrated by similes.
“Great King, is there such a thing as wind?”
“Yes, venerable sir,” he replied.
“Come now, Great King, show me the wind—whether by its color or its shape, whether as minute or gross, long or short.
“It is not possible, venerable Nāgasena, to exhibit the wind; that wind does not admit of being grasped by the hand or of being rubbed, yet nevertheless, that wind exists.”
“If, Great King, it is not possible to point out the wind, then surely there is no wind?
“I know, venerable Nāgasena, that the wind exists; this has entered my heart. Yet I am not able to point out the wind.
“In the same way, Great King, Nibbāna exists, but it is not possible to point out Nibbāna by means of its color or its shape.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! The simile is well shown, the reason is well demonstrated. It is so; thus do I accept it: ‘Nibbāna exists.
This is the fifth question, concerning whether [Nibbāna] is not born of action and so forth.
